policy: Realistic bone surfaces are a separate layer registered rigidly to the validated motion skeleton (PR #12 architecture); they never move joint centres.
No region may start detailed production bone modelling until its gate below is closed; until then only contract/test tooling and source acquisition are in scope.

Shape templates: BodyParts3D 4.0 (CC BY 4.0, single male, grade D) and OpenSim generic geometry may be used as topology/shape templates only, with any scaling recorded and justified; never as dimension targets.

Registration anchors must be derived from mesh features (e.g. sphere fit to the femoral-head patch) and compared with the skeleton within a declared budget, not declared directly (see the PR #12 review).

shoulder_girdle.gate_before_modelling: absolute SC/AC/GH centres and shoulder height relative to trunk (OPEN, coupled to U10 trunk height)

surfaces: vertebral bodies with disc-facing endplates (concavity 1.5/0.7 mm lumbar, Wang 2012)
spine.gate_before_modelling: coupled trunk candidate resolving U10 (lumbar length, trunk height) and per-level thoracic wedging

ribs_sternum.gate_before_modelling: thoracic level positions (U10) and sternum length method conflict

pelvis_hip.gate_before_modelling: sacrum position vs P1 S1 (a003 sacrum 42 mm posterior) and acetabular envelope

knee.gate_before_modelling: patellofemoral follower installed and reviewed; femur length question (412.9 mm vs ~430-437 mm context) closed

forearm_wrist_hand.gate_before_modelling: eight carpal centroids in one wrist frame; radius/ulna endpoint corridors; fingertip endpoints (H2)

foot_ankle.gate_before_modelling: tarsal contact chain (L5) and metatarsal source conflict

skull.gate_before_modelling: only movement/contact-relevant geometry; low priority for the app

female_variant: Every region keeps the same surface inventory and joint semantics; dimensions, pelvic geometry, and attachment profiles need their own sex-specific sources (none committed yet).
